title: TOTP enrolment response
description: The response to beginning a TOTP enrolment. THIS TYPE DOES NOT EXIST IN RUST — there is no TOTP enrolment response type in identity-application, identity-domain or identity-security in the bootstrap phase. What is below is the contract the identity_web API client (apps/identity/web/src/api/self-service.ts, beginTotpEnrolment) already declares as its return type, and it is recorded here so the Phase 3 work has a shape to meet and so this directory does not imply the shape exists. A schema for a type nothing can produce is a promise; this one is marked as a promise, deliberately, and it must not be read as a description of current behaviour.
x-serde-status: DEFERRED — the shape below is declared by the web client, not by any crate
x-not-yet-producible: There is no TOTP enrolment in this repository. identity-security declares factor gates as traits with no body, and there is no cryptography implemented anywhere. A client that receives this body from a working endpoint would be trusting a TOTP implementation that does not exist.

secret.description: The Base32 shared secret. A SECRET: never logged, never placed in a URL, never placed in localStorage. It is not a session token, so the HttpOnly rule that governs the session cookie does not apply to it — it must simply never be written anywhere a later reader can find it.
secret.x-handling: The UI's obligation when this day comes is to render the provisioning URI as a QR code and to treat this field the way it treats the session cookie: as a credential that is shown once and stored nowhere.

provisioning_uri.description: The otpauth:// URI to render as a QR code. It embeds `secret`, so it inherits every handling rule above: a URL is a place secrets leak from, which is why the session token is in an HttpOnly cookie and this must never be.
provisioning_uri.x-handling: render as a QR code; never log, never navigate with it, never store it

x-phase.phase: Phase 3 — Second factor, and the assurance model
x-phase.note: Phase 3's exit condition requires WebCrypto only, no cryptography crate and no hand-rolled comparison (ADR-0008), and the window and drift behaviour documented in identity-security.

x-what-phase-3-also-requires: Removing a factor is a different operation and lands in the same phase: it lowers the account's assurance, so it is the one self-service call that will demand a step-up (AAL2) when it exists. The AccountView.step_up_required flag is what tells a UI the demand is coming; a UI may warn and may not decide the answer.
